actionPlan.title: Gather and Organize Your Documents
actionPlan.description: Collect the tenancy agreement, proof of deposit payment (bank transfer record or receipt), and any written communication with your landlord.
actionPlan.userAction: Locate and safely store originals of your rental agreement and deposit payment proof.
actionPlan.source: General best practice — document organization before any dispute

actionPlan.title: Document the Move-Out
actionPlan.description: Gather any evidence of the property's condition at move-out and any key handover acknowledgement.
actionPlan.userAction: Organize move-out photos, WhatsApp/message exchanges confirming key handover, and any inspection records.

actionPlan.title: Send a Formal Written Request for Refund
actionPlan.description: Send a polite but formal written request to the landlord asking for the deposit to be returned, clearly stating the facts. Keep a copy and use a method that provides delivery confirmation.
actionPlan.userAction: Draft and send a formal written request by registered post or email. Keep the postal receipt or email delivery confirmation.
evidenceNeeded: Postal receipt or email delivery confirmation
actionPlan.source: General civil dispute best practice — formal written communication before escalation

actionPlan.title: Consider Free Legal Aid — DLSA or NALSA
actionPlan.description: If the landlord does not respond, you may approach the District Legal Services Authority (DLSA) or call the NALSA Tele-Law helpline (15100) for free legal assistance. DLSA offers free pre-litigation conciliation services.
actionPlan.userAction: Visit your local DLSA or call NALSA (15100) to understand your options and eligibility for free legal assistance.
evidenceNeeded: Copies of all your documents and correspondence
actionPlan.optionalEscalation: DLSA offers free pre-litigation conciliation. Eligibility criteria apply — check the official NALSA website.

actionPlan.title: Seek Qualified Legal Advice
actionPlan.description: If the dispute remains unresolved, consider consulting a qualified advocate or approaching the appropriate civil court. The applicable forum and procedure depend on your specific jurisdiction and facts.
actionPlan.userAction: Consult a qualified advocate or legal aid clinic to understand the appropriate legal forum and procedure for your specific situation.
actionPlan.source: General civil dispute best practice — consult a qualified legal professional
actionPlan.optionalEscalation: Applicable court procedures vary by jurisdiction and amount claimed. Verify with a qualified professional.
